content:
This chapter lists common abbreviations from handovers and care records, in alphabetical order. Use it as a quick look-up, and follow your employer’s approved abbreviation list and local policy; where they differ from this guide, they come first.

## Everyday Record Keeping

| Abbreviation | Meaning | Use or note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AKI | Acute kidney injury | Spell it out on first use in a record. |
| BP | Blood pressure | Written as a pair of readings with the unit. |
| NEWS2 | National Early Warning Score 2 | The score is recorded as a number, never as a word. |
| NMC | Nursing and Midwifery Council | The regulator for nurses and midwives in the UK. |

Take care: write “units” in full and never a bare “U”, which can be read as a zero or a four. Avoid “QD”, which can be mistaken for another frequency, and write a number such as five milligrams without a trailing zero.

## Terms That Look Alike

| Abbreviation | Meaning | Use or note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MS | Multiple sclerosis, morphine sulfate or magnesium sulfate | Ambiguous, so write the full name. |

Take care: do not use “MSO4” or “MgSO4” for the same reason. Name the medicine in full.

### Quick Check

- Follow your employer’s approved list first.
- Write units in full.
- Spell out any term that could be read two ways.
